outcome: No mathematical progress on Goodman's conjecture (general p-valent case, or any new special case) has appeared since 26 January 2024; the only in-window activity is a Lean formalization of the conjecture's statement (not a proof) in Google DeepMind's formal-conjectures repository, merged 13 September 2026.
summary: This bullet (Wikipedia's 'Goodman's conjecture on the coefficients of multivalent functions') asks whether, for p-valent functions f(z) = z + Σ b_n z^n, |b_n| is bounded by a specific linear combination of the moduli of the first p coefficients. It remains open in general as of today. I searched arXiv, Google, and the current Wikipedia article and found nothing that changes the conjecture's status since 26 January 2024: no proof, disproof, new partial case, or moved bound. The only in-window activity found anywhere is a GitHub issue (#3477, opened 8 March 2026) in Google DeepMind's 'formal-conjectures' repository tracking a Lean formalization of the conjecture's *statement*, and the corresponding pull request (#4435), which was authored by a human contributor (him1411), reviewed by a human (mo271), and merged 13 September 2026. I fetched the PR directly: it adds definitions (IsPValent, coeff, goodmanBound) and one proven sanity lemma for the trivial p=1 case (which reduces to the long-known bound |b_n| <= n, not new information), while the conjecture itself is stated with the Lean placeholder `sorry` and explicitly marked 'research open' — i.e., no proof was produced, human or machine. There is no AI system named anywhere in the issue or PR as having produced any part of this formalization; it is ordinary human-authored Lean code contributed to a benchmark/collection repository, so ai_role is 'none' and formalisation_only is true (though even calling it 'formalisation_only' is generous, since only the statement, not a proof, was formalized). The pre-2024 partial results noted in the current Wikipedia article (true for p=2,3 for functions of form P∘φ; true for p-valent typically-real functions) are unchanged and are cited only for context, not as new events. Nothing found meets even the 'partial'/'progress' bar under §3.1, so status is 'open' with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the DeepMind formalization is itself a small, event-worthy incident (an AI-focused research group choosing this conjecture as a benchmark target), which might argue for 'progress' with ai_role 'none' just to record the activity. But per §3.1 and §6.1, formalizing an open conjecture's statement without proving anything is not a change to what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry, so I classified it as 'open'/no_change_found rather than 'progress'.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or repository commit that actually discharges the `sorry` in FormalConjectures' goodman_conjecture lemma (for any nontrivial p), or a traditional journal paper proving/disproving the general conjecture or a new nontrivial special case (p >= 4, or a broader function class than typically-real/P∘φ), dated after 26 January 2024.
